scope: Known-application recipe lifecycle using actual source-owned non-GUI Node child processes and challenged IPC identity/document readback. No GUI application or native input was launched.
sourceState: Working-tree implementation; source hashes identify the tested files. Runtime temporary roots, profile paths, document paths and process IDs are deliberately omitted.

cases.name: known recipe actually launches shell:false non-GUI child with exact Unicode document and profile arguments
cases.actual: Configured executable and literal argument vector launched one source-owned child. Spaces, ampersand and Unicode remained part of one document argument. Its actual IPC response reported the configured profile and independently read document bytes; coordinator effect verification passed. Explicit created-resource disposal confirmed child exit.

cases.name: attach verifies actual PID and creation generation without launching and preserves attached resources
cases.actual: An already-running fixture was attached by explicit PID plus its observed per-instance generation. Adapter disposal left that attached process running; the test harness later cleaned its own fixture.

cases.name: invalid document paths and arbitrary executable/argument fields fail before any child exists
cases.actual: Relative paths, paths outside document roots, directories, public executable fields, arbitrary argument fields and a mismatched host environment were rejected without launching a child.

cases.name: actual process lifetime revalidation prevents stale reads and killing a PID-replacement candidate
cases.actual: A changed generation injected into the actual fixture inspector response rejected both observation and disposal; the real child remained alive. Restoring the correct inspection allowed owned disposal.

cases.name: uncertain post-launch inspection retains the owned process and never falls back to another launch
cases.actual: Inspection failure after actual spawn returned unknown delivery and cleanup. A second launch was rejected while the first child remained tracked; explicit verified disposal later cleaned it.

cases.name: wrong-generation attach is rejected without launch fallback or terminating the actual process
cases.actual: Mismatched supplied generation rejected attachment. No replacement process was launched and the actual fixture remained running.

cases.name: exact application slot selects the correct profile among ready providers of the same app
cases.actual: The registry used advertised exact windowIds to select the requested second profile rather than the higher-ranked other instance. Actual child inspection confirmed that selected profile.

cases.name: unsuccessful owned-process termination retains cleanup quarantine and cannot report ready
cases.actual: A controlled kill(false) branch retained the actual child, cleanup unknown and unavailable/quarantined diagnostics. Restoring termination allowed confirmed cleanup.

documentProof.source: Actual fixture readFile result compared independently with the harness readFile result.

ownershipProof: The test inspector challenged the actual ChildProcess IPC channel with a fresh nonce and compared PID plus a random generation created inside that running fixture. This proves that source-owned fixture instance. It does not claim generic Windows process creation-time or GUI profile inspection for arbitrary applications.
cleanup: Every test-owned fixture was explicitly disposed or cleaned by the test harness. Attached-preservation assertions occurred before harness cleanup. No user application/profile was attached or terminated.
limits: Recipes are trusted host configuration, not a sandbox. Public action payloads cannot select executable paths, arbitrary argument vectors or remote execution.
A real application recipe still needs an actual OS/app ownership inspector proving executable, process generation, profile/root and document binding. PID/name guesses are insufficient.
A document argument confirms delivery to the process, not opening/editing/saving. Verified opened-byte evidence here comes from this fixture's explicit application protocol.
Coordinator close releases use and keeps applications running. Explicit disposal terminates only the tracked created direct child after reinspection; attached processes remain open.
Launchers that exit and hand work to another process, arbitrary app document editing, unsaved-document shutdown protocols and native GUI acceptance are not established by this recipe fixture.
A new adapter receives a new logical slot generation; it cannot silently resume an old checkpoint or infer an old process from matching profile labels.
